How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.

- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Moderators started asking for this:

> As a moderator, I want to reuse my quiz at another conference, or share it with a colleague who runs Quizzy too.

The quiz page gets the "Export" link. It opens a page that shows the quiz as JSON inside a `<pre>` element (the only `<pre>` on the page), ready to copy.

`/moderate` gets the "Import quiz" button. It opens a page with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. Importing always creates a new quiz, even if a quiz with the same title exists, and opens its page.

The format:

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `questions` and `options` keep their order.
- On import, `active` is optional (`true` by default), and `correct` is optional (`false` by default).
- The export always writes both, and it writes exactly these keys: the quiz title and its questions, nothing else. The export is only for moving quiz contents.
- Imported questions follow the same rules as the question form.

When the JSON is invalid or breaks a rule, the page shows an error and nothing is imported: not the quiz, not a part of its questions.

  "output": "# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview
Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire Turbo/Stimulus) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Serving & Production Configuration
- Entrypoint: `bin/serve` prepares databases (`db:prepare`), precompiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- Plain HTTP: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, and `config.hosts.clear` in `config/environments/production.rb`.
- Persistence: All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) and Active Storage local files live under `storage/`.
- Health check: `GET /up` responds with `200` without authentication.
- Offline/Self-contained: `Inter-latin.woff2`, `quizzy.css`, and Hotwire JS modules are served locally via Propshaft and importmap with zero external network calls.

## Authentication
- Moderator endpoints live under `/moderate` (`Moderate::BaseController`) and require HTTP Basic Auth matching `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` (constant-time `secure_compare`), returning `401` on missing or invalid credentials.

## Data Model (Release 1: Preparing Quizzes)
- `Quiz` (`title`): `has_many :questions` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
- `Question` (`quiz_id`, `body`, `active`, `position`): `has_many :options` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
  - Validated and saved atomically via `Question#save_with_option_rows`: skips empty option rows, requires `body`, requires `>= 2` non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`), and requires `>= 1` correct non-empty option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`).
- `Option` (`question_id`, `text`, `correct`, `position`).

## Preview Mode
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/preview` (`Moderate::PreviewsController#show`) steps through `quiz.questions.active.ordered` one at a time using stateless query parameters (`step`, `score`, `picked`, `finished`). No preview answers are persisted to the database, cache, or session.

## Design System Classes Available for Future Releases (`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css`)
`quizzy.css` already includes component styles for upcoming live game features:
- **Moderator Runs & Responses**: `.runs-table`, `.badge--running`, `.badge--finished`, `.tabs`, `.tab`, `.response-options`, `.response-option`, `.response-card`, `.mark--right`, `.mark--wrong`, `.mark--winner`, `.pager`.
- **Big Screen Presentation (Stage)**: `.cover` (`.cover--blue`, `.cover--night`, `.cover--calm`), `.screen`, `.screen__top`, `.screen__body`, `.screen-controls`, `.lobby`, `.qr`, `.counter-pill`, `.stage-question__num`, `.stage-question__body`, `.stage-options`, `.stage-option`, `.leaderboard`, `.leader`, `.winner-banner`.
- **Mobile Participant Play**: `.play`, `.join-form`, `.waiting`, `.waiting__gem`, `.play-question__num`, `.play-question__body`, `.play-options`, `.play-option` (`.is-picked`, `.is-correct`), `.play-status` (`.play-status--right`, `.play-status--wrong`), `.result-card`.

# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview
Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire Turbo/Stimulus) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Serving & Production Configuration
- Entrypoint: `bin/serve` prepares databases (`db:prepare`), precompiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- Plain HTTP: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, and `config.hosts.clear` in `config/environments/production.rb`.
- Persistence: All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) and Active Storage local files live under `storage/`.
- Health check: `GET /up` responds with `200` without authentication.
- Offline/Self-contained: `Inter-latin.woff2`, `quizzy.css`, and Hotwire JS modules are served locally via Propshaft and importmap with zero external network calls.

## Authentication
- Moderator endpoints live under `/moderate` (`Moderate::BaseController`) and require HTTP Basic Auth matching `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` (constant-time `secure_compare`), returning `401` on missing or invalid credentials.

## Data Model (Release 1: Preparing Quizzes)
- `Quiz` (`title`): `has_many :questions` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
- `Question` (`quiz_id`, `body`, `active`, `position`): `has_many :options` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.

require "test_helper"

class ModeratorAuthAndHttpTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @orig_user = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]
    @orig_pass = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]
    ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"] = "moduser"
    ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"] = "s3cr3t-pass"

    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "RubyConf Quiz")
    @question = @quiz.questions.create!(body: "What year did Rails 1.0 ship?", active: true, position: 0)
    @opt1 = @question.options.create!(text: "2004", correct: false, position: 0)
    @opt2 = @question.options.create!(text: "2005", correct: true, position: 1)
  end

  teardown do
    ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"] = @orig_user
    ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"] = @orig_pass
  end

  def auth_headers(user = "moduser", pass = "s3cr3t-pass")
    { "HTTP_AUTHORIZATION" => ActionController::HttpAuthentication::Basic.encode_credentials(user, pass) }
  end

  test "GET /up responds with 200 without auth and accepts any host" do
    get "/up", headers: { "Host" => "arbitrary-conference-wall.local:3000" }
    assert_response :success
  end

  test "every moderator route returns 401 when credentials are missing or wrong" do
    protected_gets = [
      "/moderate",
      "/moderate/quizzes",
      "/moderate/quizzes/new",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/settings",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/new",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/#{@question.id}/edit",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/preview"
    ]

    protected_gets.each do |path|
      get path
      assert_response :unauthorized, "Expected 401 without credentials for GET #{path}"

      get path, headers: auth_headers("moduser", "wrong")
      assert_response :unauthorized, "Expected 401 with wrong password for GET #{path}"

      get path, headers: auth_headers("wrong", "s3cr3t-pass")
      assert_response :unauthorized, "Expected 401 with wrong username for GET #{path}"

      get path, headers: auth_headers.merge("Host" => "custom-host.internal")
      assert_response :success, "Expected 200 with valid credentials for GET #{path}"
    end

    post "/moderate/quizzes", params: { quiz: { title: "Blocked" } }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", params: { quiz: { title: "Blocked" } }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    delete "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    assert_response :unauthorized

    post "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions", params: { question: { body: "Blocked" } }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/#{@question.id}/move_up"
    assert_response :unauthorized

    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/#{@question.id}/toggle_active", params: { question: { active: "0" } }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    delete "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/#{@question.id}"
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "preview does not store answers in database or session" do
    quiz_count_before = Quiz.count
    question_count_before = Question.count
    option_count_before = Option.count

    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/preview",
        params: { step: 0, score: 0, picked: @opt2.id },
        headers: auth_headers
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Correct!"

    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/preview",
        params: { finished: 1, score: 1 },
        headers: auth_headers
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Score: 1/1"

    assert_equal quiz_count_before, Quiz.count
    assert_equal question_count_before, Question.count
    assert_equal option_count_before, Option.count
    assert_nil response.headers["Set-Cookie"]
  end
end

class Quiz
  class Importer
    Result = Data.define(:quiz, :errors) do
      def success?
        errors.empty? && quiz.present?
      end
    end

    def self.call(raw_json)
      new(raw_json).call
    end

    def initialize(raw_json)
      @raw_json = raw_json
    end

    def call
      return failure("Invalid JSON") unless @raw_json.is_a?(String) && !@raw_json.strip.empty?

      data = JSON.parse(@raw_json)
      return failure("Quiz JSON must be a JSON object") unless data.is_a?(Hash)

      errors = []
      title = validate_title(data, errors)
      normalized_questions = validate_questions(data, errors)

      return Result.new(quiz: nil, errors: errors) if errors.any?

      quiz = Quiz.transaction do
        created_quiz = Quiz.create!(title: title)
        normalized_questions.each_with_index do |q_attrs, q_pos|
          question = created_quiz.questions.create!(
            body: q_attrs[:text],
            active: q_attrs[:active],
            position: q_pos
          )
          q_attrs[:options].each_with_index do |opt_attrs, opt_pos|
            question.options.create!(
              text: opt_attrs[:text],
              correct: opt_attrs[:correct],
              position: opt_pos
            )
          end
        end
        created_quiz
      end

      Result.new(quiz: quiz, errors: [])
    rescue JSON::JSONError
      failure("Invalid JSON")
    end

    private

    def failure(message)
      Result.new(quiz: nil, errors: [ message ])
    end

    def validate_title(data, errors)
      raw_title = data["title"]
      if raw_title.nil? || (raw_title.is_a?(String) && raw_title.strip.empty?)
        errors << "Title can't be blank"
        nil
      elsif !raw_title.is_a?(String)
        errors << "Title must be a string"
        nil
      else
        raw_title
      end
    end

    def validate_questions(data, errors)
      raw_questions = data["questions"]
      unless raw_questions.is_a?(Array)
        errors << "Questions must be an array"
        return []
      end

      raw_questions.each_with_index.filter_map do |q_data, q_idx|
        validate_question(q_data, q_idx + 1, errors)
      end
    end

    def validate_question(q_data, q_num, errors)
      unless q_data.is_a?(Hash)
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Must be a JSON object"
        return nil
      end

      raw_text = q_data["text"]
      if raw_text.nil? || (raw_text.is_a?(String) && raw_text.strip.empty?)
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question can't be blank"
      elsif !raw_text.is_a?(String)
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question text must be a string"
      end

      active = true
      if q_data.key?("active")
        if q_data["active"] == true || q_data["active"] == false
          active = q_data["active"]
        else
          errors << "Question #{q_num}: Active must be true or false"
        end
      end

      options = validate_options(q_data["options"], q_num, errors)

      { text: raw_text, active: active, options: options }
    end

    def validate_options(raw_options, q_num, errors)
      unless raw_options.is_a?(Array)
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Options must be an array"
        return []
      end

      normalized = []
      raw_options.each_with_index do |opt_data, opt_idx|
        opt_num = opt_idx + 1
        unless opt_data.is_a?(Hash)
          errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{opt_num}: Must be a JSON object"
          next
        end

        opt_text = opt_data["text"]
        if opt_text.nil? || (opt_text.is_a?(String) && opt_text.strip.empty?)

        elsif !opt_text.is_a?(String)

      end

      if normalized.none? { |o| o[:correct] }

      end

      normalized
    end
  end
end

class Quiz
  class Importer
    Result = Data.define(:quiz, :errors) do
      def success?
        errors.empty? && quiz.present?
      end
    end

    def self.call(raw_json)
      new(raw_json).call
    end

    def initialize(raw_json)
      @raw_json = raw_json
    end

    def call
      return failure("Invalid JSON") unless @raw_json.is_a?(String) && !@raw_json.strip.empty?

      data = JSON.parse(@raw_json)
      return failure("Quiz JSON must be a JSON object") unless data.is_a?(Hash)

      errors = []
      title = validate_title(data, errors)
      normalized_questions = validate_questions(data, errors)

      return Result.new(quiz: nil, errors: errors) if errors.any?

      quiz = Quiz.transaction do
        created_quiz = Quiz.create!(title: title)
        normalized_questions.each_with_index do |q_attrs, q_pos|
          question = created_quiz.questions.create!(
            body: q_attrs[:text],
            active: q_attrs[:active],
            position: q_pos
          )
          q_attrs[:options].each_with_index do |opt_attrs, opt_pos|
            question.options.create!(
              text: opt_attrs[:text],
              correct: opt_attrs[:correct],
              position: opt_pos
            )
          end
        end
        created_quiz
      end

      Result.new(quiz: quiz, errors: [])
    rescue JSON::JSONError
      failure("Invalid JSON")
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
      Result.new(quiz: nil, errors: e.record.errors.full_messages)
    end

    private

    def failure(message)
      Result.new(quiz: nil, errors: [ message ])
    end

    def validate_title(data, errors)
      raw_title = data["title"]
      if raw_title.nil? || (raw_title.is_a?(String) && raw_title.strip.empty?)
        errors << "Title can't be blank"
        nil
      elsif !raw_title.is_a?(String)
        errors << "Title must be a string"
        nil
      else
        raw_title
      end
    end

    def validate_questions(data, errors)
      raw_questions = data["questions"]
      unless raw_questions.is_a?(Array)
        errors << "Questions must be an array"
        return []
      end

      raw_questions.each_with_index.filter_map do |q_data, q_idx|
        validate_question(q_data, q_idx + 1, errors)
      end
    end

    def validate_question(q_data, q_num, errors)
      unless q_data.is_a?(Hash)
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Must be a JSON object"
        return nil
      end

      raw_text = q_data["text"]
      if raw_text.nil? || (raw_text.is_a?(String) && raw_text.strip.empty?)
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question can't be blank"
      elsif !raw_text.is_a?(String)
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question text must be a string"
      end

      active = true
      if q_data.key?("active")
        if q_data["active"] == true || q_data["active"] == false
          active = q_data["active"]
        else
          errors << "Question #{q_num}: Active must be true or false"
        end
      end

      options = validate_options(q_data["options"], q_num, errors)

      { text: raw_text, active: active, options: options }
    end

    def validate_options(raw_options, q_num, errors)
      unless raw_options.is_a?(Array)
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Options must be an array"
        return []
      end

      normalized = []
      raw_options.each_with_index do |opt_data, opt_idx|
        opt_num = opt_idx + 1
        unless opt_data.is_a?(Hash)
          errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{opt_num}: Must be a JSON object"
          next
        end

        opt_text = opt_data["text"]
        if opt_text.nil? || (opt_text.is_a?(String) && opt_text.strip.empty?)
          errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{opt_num}: Option text can't be blank"
        elsif !opt_text.is_a?(String)
          errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{opt_num}: Option text must be a string"
        end

        opt_correct = false
        if opt_data.key?("correct")
          if opt_data["correct"] == true || opt_data["correct"] == false
            opt_correct = opt_data["correct"]
          else
            errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{opt_num}: Correct must be true or false"
          end
        end

        normalized << { text: opt_text, correct: opt_correct }
      end

      if raw_options.size < 2
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Add at least two options"
      end

      if normalized.none? { |o| o[:correct] }
        errors << "Question #{q_num}: Mark at least one option as correct"
      end

      normalized
    end
  end
end
EOF

# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview
Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire Turbo/Stimulus) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Serving & Production Configuration
- Entrypoint: `bin/serve` prepares databases (`db:prepare`), precompiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- Plain HTTP: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, and `config.hosts.clear` in `config/environments/production.rb`.
- Persistence: All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) and Active Storage local files live under `storage/`.
- Health check: `GET /up` responds with `200` without authentication.
- Offline/Self-contained: `Inter-latin.woff2`, `quizzy.css`, and Hotwire JS modules are served locally via Propshaft and importmap with zero external network calls.

## Authentication
- Moderator endpoints live under `/moderate` (`Moderate::BaseController`) and require HTTP Basic Auth matching `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` (constant-time `secure_compare`), returning `401` on missing or invalid credentials.

## Data Model (Preparing Quizzes)
- `Quiz` (`title`): `has_many :questions` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
- `Question` (`quiz_id`, `body`, `active`, `position`): `has_many :options` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
  - Validated and saved atomically via `Question#save_with_option_rows`: skips empty option rows, requires `body`, requires `>= 2` non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`), and requires `>= 1` correct non-empty option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`).
- `Option` (`question_id`, `text`, `correct`, `position`).

## Quiz Export & Import
- **Export** (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export`, `Moderate::ExportsController#show`):
  - Renders `Quiz#to_export_json` inside a single `<pre class="code-block">` element.
  - `Quiz#as_export_json` writes **only** `"title"` and `"questions"` (`"text"`, `"active"`, `"options"` -> `"text"`, `"correct"`), preserving `questions` and `options` order. Do not include IDs, timestamps, or future game run/response data: export is strictly for moving quiz contents.
- **Import** (`GET/POST /moderate/quizzes/import`, `Moderate::ImportsController`, `Quiz::Importer`):
  - Validates JSON structure and all quiz/question/option rules upfront and creates the new `Quiz`, `Question`s, and `Option`s atomically inside a single transaction.
  - `active` defaults to `true` when omitted; `correct` defaults to `false` when omitted.
  - Always creates a new `Quiz` even if a quiz with the same `title` already exists, then redirects (`303`) to the newly created quiz page.

## Preview Mode
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/preview` (`Moderate::PreviewsController#show`) steps through `quiz.questions.active.ordered` one at a time using stateless query parameters (`step`, `score`, `picked`, `finished`). No preview answers are persisted to the database, cache, or session.

## Design System Classes Available for Future Releases (`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css`)
`quizzy.css` already includes component styles for upcoming live game features:
- **Moderator Runs & Responses**: `.runs-table`, `.badge--running`, `.badge--finished`, `.tabs`, `.tab`, `.response-options`, `.response-option`, `.response-card`, `.mark--right`, `.mark--wrong`, `.mark--winner`, `.pager`.

I have implemented quiz JSON export and import for moderators in Quizzy:

- **Export (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export`)**: Added the `"Export"` link on the quiz page, opening a page that displays the quiz JSON inside a single `<pre>` element (`Quiz#to_export_json`) with only `"title"` and `"questions"` (`"text"`, `"active"`, `"options"` with `"text"` and `"correct"`), preserving `questions` and `options` order.
- **Import (`GET/POST /moderate/quizzes/import`)**: Added the `"Import quiz"` button on `/moderate`, opening a page with the `"Quiz JSON"` `<textarea>` and `"Import"` button. `Quiz::Importer` defaults omitted `active` to `true` and omitted `correct` to `false`, validates the JSON structure and all quiz/question/option rules atomically before persisting inside a transaction, always creates a new quiz even if a quiz with the same title exists, and redirects to the new quiz page (or renders validation errors with `422` without importing anything).
- **Tests & Documentation**: Added model, HTTP auth integration, and end-to-end Chromium system tests, and updated `docs/architecture.md`.
